newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian state begins evacuation ahead of storm.
newsitem.headline: Indian state begins evacuation ahead of storm.

text.p: Thousands of people began to evacuate India's eastern Andhra Pradesh state on Saturday as the second cyclonic storm in three weeks threatened to lash its coast, officials said.
State Relief Commissioner H.S. Brahma said officials in nine coastal areas of fishing villages and rice and oilseed farms had been asked to help in the evacuation.

A total of 971 people were killed and 925 were missing after a cyclone hit the coast on November 7. More than 177,000 people were evacuated from the worst affected areas, which suffered an estimated $1.4 billion worth of damage.

Indian meterological authorities in New Delhi said a deep depression lay in the Bay of Bengal about 550 km (335 miles) southeast of Machlipatnam, Andhra Pradesh, and was likely to move north-northeast.
Heavy rain was expected in Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu and Kerala states, a meterological department statement said.

"The deep depression slightly moved north-northeastwards and again became practically stationary," C.V.V. Brahma, director of the meterological centre in Hyderabad, Andhra Pradesh's capital, told Reuters.
"We are keeping a watch," he said.
The United News of India quoted Andhra Pradesh Revenue Minister Devender Goud on Friday as saying state authorities had asked the army, navy and air force to help the evacuation.
Officials on the coast hoisted danger signals and urged fishermen not to put out to sea. The navy and coastguard were asked to warn fishermen at sea to return home.
